public_rationale: The claim is that benchmark success is only a limited indicator of general intelligence. Two studies from before the 2026-02-17 post meet the contract's support condition. The GSM-Symbolic study (Mirzadeh et al., first posted 2024-10-07, ICLR 2025) found that the performance of all models tested declined when only the numbers in GSM8K-style questions changed. Adding one clause that seemed relevant but did not bear on the answer cut performance by up to 65%. 'The Leaderboard Illusion' (Singh et al., preprint, 2025-04-29) found that extra Chatbot Arena data gave relative gains of up to 112% on the arena distribution. The authors concluded that these dynamics produced 'overfitting to Arena-specific dynamics rather than general model quality'. The packet has no evidence that benchmark success reliably tracks robust general capability.
limitations: 'General intelligence' has no agreed measure. Neither study measures it directly. They show benchmark scores overstating robustness or reflecting benchmark-specific effects.
The evidence covers two cases, GSM8K-style maths questions and the Chatbot Arena leaderboard, not benchmarks in general.
The Leaderboard Illusion is a preprint, and its 112% figure is the authors' own conservative estimate of gains on the arena distribution.
'Limited indicator' has no threshold, so the claim is partly conceptual.

So benchmark scores alone are a weak guide to general intelligence.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that benchmark success reliably tracks robust general capability under novel conditions, with little gap between benchmark and perturbed or real-world performance.
